chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fudalah from Aban from Isma'il ibn al-Fadl said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who gives charity) about a man who donates part of his wealth during his lifetime in every manner of goodness, and says: 'If I need something from my wealth or its yield, I am more entitled to it.' Is that permissible for him, having dedicated it to God? And what is his state when the man dies? Does it return as inheritance or does it remain as charity? He said: 'It returns as inheritance to his family.'
ai.seo_question: Does partial charity given during life return to heirs or stay as charity after death?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the fiqh of 'partial charity' (sadaqah muqayyadah) where the donor retains usufruct or reclamation rights, establishing that such wealth remains part of the donor's estate rather than becoming irrevocably transferred. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) rules that upon death, the asset reverts to the heirs as inheritance, highlighting the distinction between full gift (hibah) and conditional charity in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling ensures that donors can utilize their wealth for personal needs during life without forfeiting their right to pass it on to their lineage.
